terms.meaning: A trial that shows what an import would do without actually saving anything.
One row of project data, such as a single project and its details.
Saving the checked data to the database for real.
A shared store that keeps fetched data so pages update without reloading everything.

used_by: Not visible in the code shown.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared setup
sections.what: Brings in the icons, the card layout, the industry list, the server request helper and the shared data cache key used to refresh project data.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cache key is imported so the page can refresh project data after an import.
sections.watch_out: If the shared cache key changes, the refresh after an import will stop updating the right data.

sections.name: IssueDetail
sections.title: Problem detail shape
sections.what: Describes one problem found in a record: whether it is an error or a warning, which field it concerns, and a message explaining it.
sections.why: Likely reason: separating errors from warnings lets the page block bad data while still showing advisory notes.
sections.watch_out: Only the two level names are allowed, so any new level needs this type changed too.

sections.name: IssueItem
sections.title: Problems grouped by record
sections.what: Groups the problems for one record, along with the record's name, which may be missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: so each record can be listed with its own problems in the review screen.
sections.watch_out: The name can be empty, so any code showing it must handle a missing name.

sections.name: DryRunPlan
sections.title: Shape of the preview result
sections.what: Describes the summary the server returns after a preview: how many records are new, updated, unchanged, errored or in conflict, plus evidence counts and sub-industry totals. Nothing is saved at this stage.
sections.why: Lets the admin review the changes before anything is committed.
sections.watch_out: Field names must match the server response exactly, or the screen shows blanks or zeros.

sections.name: CommitResult, NA
sections.title: Shape of the saved result and the N/A label
sections.what: Describes the summary returned after a commit, showing what was actually written. Also defines a small grey N/A label that the screen reuses for missing values.
sections.why: Keeps the final result separate from the preview so each stage is clear.
sections.watch_out: The N/A label is only styled text, so seeing it does not by itself prove a value is missing.

sections.name: parseRecords
sections.title: Checks the pasted or uploaded JSON
sections.what: Reads the text in the box and turns it into a list of records. It accepts a plain list or an object with a records list, and rejects empty input, invalid JSON or an empty list with a clear message.
sections.why: Catches bad input before anything is sent to the server.
sections.watch_out: It only checks that the top level is a list. It does not check each record's fields, so the server has to do that.

sections.name: StatTile
sections.title: Small number tile
sections.what: Shows a labelled number, such as the count of new records. For problem tiles it turns red when the count is above zero.
sections.why: Makes counts easy to scan and draws attention to problems.
sections.watch_out: Red only applies when the tile is a problem tile and the value is above zero, so a zero count stays neutral.

sections.name: Ingest (part 1)
sections.title: Page memory and file loading
sections.what: Keeps the page's state: the chosen industry, paste or upload mode, the text, the preview plan, and any error. It also reads a chosen file into the text box and clears any old preview when the input changes.
sections.why: The code comment says this ensures the admin can never commit records that differ from what was previewed.
sections.watch_out: Every edit clears the preview, so the admin must preview again before committing.

sections.name: Ingest (part 2)
sections.title: Preview and commit actions
sections.what: Sends the records to the server for a dry run and shows the plan, or an error message if it fails. Commit sends the same previewed records, then refreshes the portfolio and project views.
sections.why: Committing the previewed records means the approved plan is what actually runs.
sections.watch_out: If a commit fails, the confirmation closes but the plan stays on screen, and no saved result is shown.

sections.name: Ingest (part 3)
sections.title: Rules for enabling the Commit button
sections.what: Decides when Commit can be pressed: a plan must exist, no commit may have happened yet, the industry must match the preview, and at least one insert, update or evidence item must be planned. Preview is disabled when the text box is empty.
sections.why: Prevents committing with an outdated preview or with nothing to change.
sections.watch_out: Evidence items count toward the check, so an evidence-only change also enables Commit.

sections.name: Ingest (part 4)
sections.title: Page header and source input choices
sections.what: Draws the top bar with links to the industry directory and Data Quality, then the Source Records box with an industry picker and a choice between paste and upload.
sections.why: Gives the admin a clear way to choose the industry and the input method.
sections.watch_out: Changing the industry clears any previous preview, by design.

sections.name: Ingest (part 5)
sections.title: File picker, text box and help text
sections.what: Shows the file chooser in upload mode, the JSON text box, and help text describing the required and optional fields. Shows any error message below the box.
sections.why: Explains the expected record shape so inputs arrive in the right form.
sections.watch_out: The help text describes the format by hand and can fall out of step with the server's rules.

sections.name: Ingest (part 6)
sections.title: Preview and commit buttons and result tiles
sections.what: Draws the Preview and Commit buttons with their disabled states, and a hint when there is nothing to commit. After a commit it shows a panel of count tiles and a link to Data Quality.
sections.why: Gives the admin clear actions and a clear record of what was written.
sections.watch_out: Preview is disabled whenever the text box is empty, so a box holding only spaces also blocks it.

sections.name: Ingest (part 7)
sections.title: Dry-run plan summary and evidence notes
sections.what: Shows the plan after a preview: count tiles for total, new, updated, unchanged, evidence, errors and conflicts. It also notes how many evidence items were skipped as missing a required field or as duplicates.
sections.why: Lets the admin judge the change before committing.
sections.watch_out: The note gives counts of skipped evidence but does not list which items were skipped, so the source file must be checked for those.

sections.name: Ingest (part 8)
sections.title: Sub-industry breakdown and problem list header
sections.what: Lists how many eligible records fall into each sub-industry, with a placeholder for records that have none. Then it starts the errored and conflicts panel with its count.
sections.why: Helps the admin spot unexpected groupings.
sections.watch_out: The problem count adds errors and conflicts together, so the number alone does not say which kind.

sections.name: Ingest (part 9)
sections.title: Problem rows table
sections.what: Shows a table of errored and conflicting records, with a label for each kind, the record name, and a list of issues per field.
sections.why: Lets the admin find and fix bad records in the source data.
sections.watch_out: Records with no name show a placeholder, which can make them hard to find in the source file.

sections.name: Ingest (part 10)
sections.title: Warnings summary panel
sections.what: Shows a card listing records that did not map cleanly during import. It shows a total count, chips for each problem field sorted from most to least common, and a list of each affected record with its specific issues. If there are no warnings, it shows a message saying all eligible records mapped cleanly.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user needs to see what the import would skip or get wrong before committing, so the warnings appear inside the review screen.
sections.watch_out: A record with no name falls back to a placeholder, and the list keys combine the name with the position, so the same name can appear more than once.

sections.name: Ingest (part 11)
sections.title: Commit confirmation dialog
sections.what: Opens a pop-up that states the industry database that will be written to, and the counts of rows to insert, rows to update, and evidence rows to add. The user can cancel, or press Confirm and Commit, which starts the write. The commit button is disabled and shows a spinner while the write runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: writing to the database is hard to undo, so the user must see the exact effect and confirm it first.
sections.watch_out: The disabled state only blocks repeat clicks while committing, so any change to how the write starts must keep this confirmation step in front of it.

summary: Admin page for importing project records, which checks them and lists any problems before anything is saved. Only the first 25 lines were visible.
purpose: Likely reason: lets an administrator bring in new project data safely by seeing a plan and problems first.
why: Likely reason: the types and imports point to a check-then-commit flow, with a dry run before a real save.
how: 1. Reads records from pasted text or an uploaded file. 2. Checks each record and collects problems, each marked as an error or a warning. 3. Shows a dry-run plan and the problems grouped by record. 4. Sends the records to the server on confirmation. Only the first 25 lines were visible, so the exact steps are unknown beyond these likely ones.
inputs: Pasted text or an uploaded file of project records, and the list of industries.
outputs: A dry-run plan, lists of problems, and a commit result once the import is sent. The data format is not visible.
risks: Problems marked as warnings may still be saved, so an administrator must read them. The page sends data to the server, so a mistaken import could add wrong projects.
debug: If records are rejected, read the problem list for the field and message. If a save fails, check the request helper and the server response. The import logic was not visible, so read the parsing and commit code directly.
